ratings_why.fun: Wearing the shop's best text and watching Guised Changelings grow is a joy to draft, but the board carries two or more texts per unit and swings with the lobby.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7: it is the only tribe that trades with the shop, steals enemy text, and joins other tribes through its Guises, so it plays unlike anything in the game.

verdict_why: The fantasy and the reads are mostly there; the Fetch and the Weeks-Old Hob each need one line to say what they do.

points.text: The Fetch copies your biggest unit's 'stats and Guise', but if the carry is not a Changeling it has no Guise, so the Stock is a blank body; the builds call it a copy of your carry. Say whether the Stock wears the carry itself as its Guise.
Weeks-Old Hob takes its Guise when played, so on that turn it never 'kept the same Guise all turn'. Say whether the turn it is played counts.
Each Changeling reads as its own line plus a borrowed tag; keep Guise text visibly secondary (a tag with the source card's art) so a seven-unit board stays readable at a glance.
The Lady can hold five texts; show her as a stack of small source portraits rather than five text lines, which also sells 'nobody has seen her as herself'.
Grandfer Acorn is a plain buffer; his eggshell tell could show in play, such as a small gain each time he is unmasked by a Guise changing on him.

standouts.why: Penny Second takes the enemy's text and leaves it blank: the duchess turned away as the impostor, in one clear line.
Pip Unlike's mirror-backwards copy is the folklore made into a rule, and it opens a real second Pass lane.
Wicker Moll leaving a Stock that wears the departed unit is the changeling swap, read at a glance.

weakest.why: Coat-Peg Steward asks the player to track which stats were 'gained' on an invisible ledger; hard to read and little flavour.
Placement Officer is a repeat of the Clerk on a timer; it adds no new picture.
The Matron's tribe-counting buff is generic and needs the reader to check each Changeling's borrowed tribe.

flags.note: What the Stock wears when your biggest unit is not a Changeling.
Whether the turn it is played counts as keeping its Guise all turn.
With the Keeper of the Lost Hour she doubles many stolen fight texts in one body; the high roll worth the owner's eye.
